title: Merge Triplets to Form Target Triplet
description:
# Merge Triplets to Form Target Triplet

A **triplet** is an array of exactly three integers. You are given a list `triplets`, where `triplets[i] = [ai, bi, ci]`, and a target triplet `target = [x, y, z]`.

You may merge one triplet into another any number of times. Merging `[a, b, c]` with `[d, e, f]` produces `[max(a, d), max(b, e), max(c, f)]`.

Return `true` if it is possible to make `target` appear as one of the triplets after zero or more merges. Return `false` otherwise.

## Example 1:

**Input:** triplets = [[2,5,3],[1,8,4],[1,7,5]], target = [2,7,5]
**Output:** true
**Explanation:** Ignore [1,8,4] because its second coordinate exceeds the target. The remaining safe triplets can provide target coordinates 2, 7, and 5.

## Example 2:

**Input:** triplets = [[3,4,5],[4,5,6]], target = [3,2,5]
**Output:** false
**Explanation:** No safe triplet can provide the second target coordinate 2.

## Example 3:

**Input:** triplets = [[2,5,3],[2,3,4],[1,2,5],[5,2,3]], target = [5,5,5]
**Output:** true
**Explanation:** Safe triplets can provide target coordinates 5 in the first, second, and third positions, so repeated coordinate-wise maximum merges can form [5,5,5].

## Constraints:

*   `1 <= triplets.length <= 10^5`
*   `triplets[i].length == target.length == 3`
*   `1 <= ai, bi, ci, x, y, z <= 1000`

solutions.name: Greedy Coordinate Coverage
solutions.description:
## Approach
Scan all triplets. Skip any triplet that exceeds the target in at least one coordinate. For every safe triplet, mark which target coordinates it matches exactly. Return true once all three coordinates have been covered.

## Key Insight
A merge is coordinate-wise maximum, so a coordinate that goes above the target can never be lowered later. Among only safe triplets, every covered target coordinate can be supplied independently and then merged together.

## Complexity Analysis
The algorithm scans the list once and checks three coordinates per triplet, so the time complexity is O(n). It stores only three booleans, so the space complexity is O(1).

solutions.name: Bitmask Filtering
solutions.description:
## Approach
Represent the three target coordinates with bits 0, 1, and 2. For each safe triplet, OR in the bits for coordinates that match the target. If the mask becomes `111b`, the target can be formed.

## Key Insight
This is the same coverage proof compressed into a small integer. The unsafe-triplet filter is still the essential step: a bit should count only if that triplet can safely participate in the final merge.

## Complexity Analysis
Each triplet is visited once, so the time complexity is O(n). The mask is a single integer, so the space complexity is O(1).

solutions.name: Explicit Safe Triplet Merge
solutions.description:
## Approach
Filter out unsafe triplets, then explicitly merge every remaining triplet into a running coordinate-wise maximum. At the end, compare the merged triplet with the target.

## Key Insight
After removing unsafe triplets, taking the maximum of all safe triplets is the strongest triplet that can be formed without overshooting. If even that maximum is not the target, no subset of safe triplets can do better.

## Complexity Analysis
The scan performs constant work per triplet, so the time complexity is O(n). The running merged triplet has length three, so the space complexity is O(1).

solutions.name: Independent Coordinate Witness Scan
solutions.description:
## Approach
Check the three target coordinates one at a time. For each coordinate, scan for at least one safe triplet whose value equals the target in that coordinate. If any coordinate has no safe witness, return false.

## Key Insight
The final triplet needs one safe witness for each coordinate, not necessarily the same witness. Because the triplet length is fixed at three, three independent scans are still linear and make the proof condition explicit.

## Complexity Analysis
There are exactly three scans over the list, so the time complexity is O(3n), which simplifies to O(n). The algorithm uses only loop variables, so the space complexity is O(1).

solutions.name: Constructive Witness Merge
solutions.description:
## Approach
Store one safe witness triplet for each target coordinate. After the scan, explicitly merge the saved witnesses and compare the constructed result with the target.

## Key Insight
This version turns the existence proof into a construction. If every coordinate has a safe witness, merging just those at most three witnesses is enough; if a coordinate has no safe witness, no sequence of maximum merges can create it.

## Complexity Analysis
The list is scanned once and at most three witness references are stored, so the time complexity is O(n) and the space complexity is O(1).
